newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Netcare NTC.J gets control stake in Clinic.
newsitem.headline: Netcare NTC.J gets control stake in Clinic.

text.p: Hospital management company Network Healthcare Holdings Ltd (Netcare) said on Sunday it had acquired a controlling interest in Clinic Holdings Limited (Clinics).
Netcare said in a statement it had reached an agreement with Clinics majority shareholder and founder Barney Hurwitz to acquire his controlling interest in the company.
As an integral part of the acquisition, Netcare has invited various strategic black economic empowerment groups, including three unions, to participate as shareholders of Netcare.
The deal will be financed through substantial investment by Fedsure, all of the black empowerment partners, and through certain rights offers both in Netcare and Clinics.
"Fedsure is the largest shareholder in Netcare and intends to increase its shareholder stake to about 25 percent," the statement said.

Netcare, whose founder shareholders are doctors, was listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in December 1996. It owns and manages seven hospitals with a total of 790 beds. Its recently released 1997 interim results reflect a 116 percent increase in turnover for the comparable period in 1996.
The share has traded successfully, more than doubling its price in four months. The company is ungeared and has cash resources worth 25 million rand ($5.5 million).
Clinics owns 17 hospitals and manages an additional eight, privately owned by Hurwitz, with a total of 4,760 beds.

The unlisted operations comprising eight hospitals will be acquired for 127.4 million rand. These hospitals are at various stages of profit maturity and currently generate earnings of 10.8 million rand. They will be degeared at the time of purchase and their growth in earnings is expected to increase significantly in the next few years.
Netcare intends to immediately implement its vision and management values into Clinic's hospitals and improve their margins, working capital and asset management.
On completion of the transaction, the merged group will have a turnover in excess of 1.6 billion rand, with projected operating profits of 280 million rand.
